USER-GUIDE.md:
# Atelier 1.0 — Your study space in Anki

Organize your classes, build cards from your sources, prepare for exams, and make Anki feel like your own space. Atelier includes Card Studio, Exam Studio, Pip, and twelve visual worlds. Onigiri is optional.

## Install or update

Save your work and finish any import or card-adding operation. In an active practice session, choose **Save & close**. Back up your Anki collection and the local Atelier, exam, and source data described below.

In Anki, open **Tools → Add-ons → Install from file**, choose **Atelier-1.0.0.ankiaddon**, and restart Anki completely. Keep the file intact; do not unzip it. Install over your existing Atelier rather than deleting it. Your current appearance, widgets, groups, and saved work are retained.

Keep any separate **Exam Sprout** or **Workshop** add-on disabled. Their features are included here. Do not delete their data. Other add-ons, including Onigiri, can stay installed.

Confirm **Tools → Atelier · 1.0.0**. This release targets Windows desktop Anki **26.08.1** with the standard editor. Experimental editors, Anki beta releases, macOS, Linux, and specialized add-on combinations are not part of the verified support target. This desktop add-on does not install on AnkiMobile, AnkiDroid, or AnkiWeb. Cards added to Anki can sync normally; your device still needs to support their card template and media.

## Start with what you need today

**Study desk** is your home. Add cards, Browse, and Sync remain easy to reach. **Continue your work** brings back unfinished drafts, repairs, and saved practice. **Library** contains your Anki decks; **Sources & projects** contains the documents you use to build cards.

To study a class, find its folder in Library and set it as an active study. Open that group to choose a lecture. **Quick study** uses your usual Anki schedule and studies one lecture at a time. Studying a whole parent folder is a separate, clearly labelled action. Removing a group removes its shortcut, not its cards or their due dates.

## Build cards with Card Studio

Choose **Add cards**. Create or choose a source project, then write a question and answer, import a document, or work from an image. A source project keeps the document and your drafts together; it is not another Anki deck.

Card Studio saves drafts locally. A saved draft is **not yet in Anki**. Choose **Review & add this draft**, check its destination, note/card counts, and any duplicate or field-mapping warnings, then confirm adding it. **Drafts & approval** is the inbox for unfinished cards from all projects.

For an image, use **Mask Studio** to cover the parts you want to recall. Figure previews load as you reach them; masks and attachments use the original image, not the thumbnail. PDF page rendering requires Qt PDF in your Anki installation. PowerPoint and Word imports preserve extracted content and embedded figures; they do not promise an exact slide/page reproduction. Attach a matching PDF when original layout matters.

From a deck’s page, **Add cards here** selects that destination for the editor. Specialized note types and editor extensions can use **Tools → Atelier → Card Studio → Add cards in native Anki…**.

## Plan an exam

Open **Exam Studio**, name your exam, choose its decks, and set your routine. The form is saved at its final **Save** step; leaving unfinished setup asks for confirmation. Active study folders are quick links for normal review, while an exam plan also contains the date and practice settings.

**Build exam plan** inside a source project selects its linked notes. Review the exact material before saving. It does not automatically add a plan or expand a document into an entire class.

## Practice without changing normal reviews

**Practice & mocks** uses your existing Anki cards. Choose the question count, time limit, and material, preview the actual selection, then start. Independent practice and self-marking do not change the cards’ Anki schedules.

A simulated exam keeps answers hidden until submission. The question map, flags, confidence, and written responses help you review afterward. **Save & close** stores an unfinished session for resumption. Merely closing a window is not a promise that responses are saved. A timed exam’s deadline continues while it is closed; saving does not pause the clock.

Results summarize your self-marks, not a predicted exam grade. Planning/readiness estimates are guidance, not a validated forecast. Your recorded Anki reviews and independent practice results remain separate.

## Study with Pip

**Pip Study** can use an active study group or a saved exam plan. You do not need to create a duplicate plan for an existing group.

Check the **Introduce new cards** setting before starting. With it off, the session is independent rehearsal. With it enabled, eligible new cards can receive real Anki ratings after you reveal the answer. Previously learned cards remain rehearsal. Pip’s petting and watering are separate from study progress.

## Make the home yours

Choose **Appearance** to select a world, spacing, motion, reviewer context, and supported Anki-window styling. The same world follows you through planning, practice, and card building. Custom interactive cards and occlusion masks retain their original layout. Use **Controls only** or **Original Anki** reviewer styling for a specialist template when needed.

**Widgets → Arrange widgets** adds, removes, reorders, and sizes your widgets. **Show on Study desk** also places a chosen widget on the main home. Choose **Save layout** to keep changes. **My note** saves when you choose **Save note**. Removing its widget does not erase the note.

Widgets work without Onigiri. Compatible installed add-ons can offer optional widgets. **More tools → Onigiri rewards — original page** opens Onigiri’s actual game and widgets when available; the **Atelier widgets** return takes you back to the built-in page. **Original Onigiri / other theme** lets that add-on keep control of its home and reviewer.

## Review progress, export, and sync

**Study progress** shows 7 or 30 Anki study days for your selected material. Answer events can include repeated answers to one card; they are not the same as distinct cards. Again percentage is not retention or mastery. The full Anki Statistics window remains available.

**Export cards** lets you search decks and put active classes first, then opens Anki’s own export options. Choosing a parent includes its subdecks. Selecting a deck does not write a file until you confirm in Anki.

**Sync** uses Anki’s normal synchronization. It does not include all local exam plans, source projects, drafts, widget notes, or Atelier preferences. **Anki tools** keeps Import, Export, note types, collection checks, preferences, profiles, Undo/Redo, and other original tools available.

## Back up all of your work

Anki’s collection backup is important, but it is not a complete Atelier backup. Close Anki before manually copying files. Keep these together:

- Your normal Anki collection and media backup.
- Atelier’s **user_files** folder inside its add-on installation. In **Tools → Add-ons**, select Atelier and choose **View Files**.
- Your Anki profile’s **exam_sprout** folder for exam records, saved sessions, and Pip effort.
- Your Anki profile’s complete **workshop** folder, including its database **and sources**. The database alone is not a complete source backup.

The Anki profile normally lives under `%APPDATA%\Anki2\<profile name>` on Windows. A custom data-folder launch can use another location. Keep backups outside the live profile and verify that they contain the expected files.

## When something is wrong

Use **Tools → Atelier** for original-home/reviewer recovery, widget recovery, and display diagnostics. Diagnostics are not sent automatically; review them before sharing, because error reports can contain file paths. Never include an API key or a private document unless you deliberately intend to share it.

To disable Atelier, use the Add-ons window and restart. Disable rather than delete it so your local preferences remain. To return to separate Sprout/Workshop installations, first disable the combined Atelier and restart; do not run two independent copies against the same data folders.

Before rolling back, save work and back up all stores. This release does not change the existing exam/source storage formats.

## Privacy and optional assistance

There is no telemetry or automatic diagnostic upload. Manual creation, search, and studying need no AI service. Optional provider assistance requires configuration and approval of the outgoing text. Suggestions remain drafts and must be reviewed before being added to Anki. Provider fees and policies apply. See **PRIVACY.md** for the full data and network boundaries.

# Atelier 1.0 — Study, create, and organize

For appearance settings, use **Tools → Atelier → Appearance & compatibility** instead of editing this file. Choose a world, adjust spacing and motion, and decide how your reviewer and supported Anki tool windows look.

**Widgets → Arrange widgets** customizes the Widgets page. Select **Show on Study desk** to put a widget on the main home too. Choose **Save layout** to keep changes. Onigiri is not required.

Exam Studio and Card Studio are included. Keep separate Exam Sprout and Workshop installations disabled, without deleting their data. Your existing plans, sources, drafts, and widget settings are kept.

**Sync updates your Anki collection, not all local Atelier data.** Back up Atelier's `user_files` plus your Anki profile's `exam_sprout` and complete `workshop` folders. See **USER-GUIDE.md** for everyday workflows, backups, and recovery.

Normal review uses your Anki schedule. Independent practice does not reschedule cards. Pip's explicitly enabled **Introduce new cards** mode can submit real ratings for eligible new cards after reveal.

Atelier 1.0.0 targets Windows desktop Anki 26.08.1. Specialized templates and other add-ons may need their own settings. Use the original-reviewer recovery action when required; do not remove your data to change appearance.

RELEASE-NOTES.md:
# Atelier 1.0.0

**A complete study space for Anki: organize, create, prepare, and review.**

Atelier 1.0 brings the integrated study, organization, and card-building tools into one release. It keeps the layout and primary workflows accepted in 0.9.0-rc6. The final pass updates version information and user-facing explanations, not the assessment, card-building, or storage algorithms.

## Included

Twelve visual worlds; a complete home with Add cards, Browse, and Sync; a searchable library with natural sorting and active study groups; independent customizable widgets; study progress and active-first export selection; Card Studio with sources, drafts, image masks and approval; Exam Studio with planning, practice, written responses, saved sessions and results; and Pip with clearly labelled rehearsal or new-card learning.

Original Anki tools remain available. Onigiri is optional and has its own explicit original-page route. Specialized card designs retain their appropriate rendering and editing paths.

## What changed from 0.9.0-rc6

- Atelier now identifies itself as **1.0.0** in its installation metadata, menus, and interface.
- Appearance, widget, progress, export, and card-building explanations use clearer everyday language.
- Exam Studio no longer calls the integrated release a preview or exposes development wording as product instructions.
- Updated user guide, installation/recovery instructions, privacy details, and release documentation.
- Accepted layouts, icons, world artwork, defaults, store locations, and primary action routes are unchanged.

## Install or update

Save and close work and wait for imports/card adding to finish. Back up the collection, Atelier's `user_files`, and the profile-local `exam_sprout` and complete `workshop` folders. Keep standalone Sprout and Workshop disabled.

Use **Tools → Add-ons → Install from file**, select **Atelier-1.0.0.ankiaddon**, and restart Anki completely. Do not unzip the file or delete the existing Atelier installation. Confirm **Tools → Atelier · 1.0.0**. Existing records, preferences, and widget layouts are reused without a new migration.

## Good to know

**Windows desktop Anki 26.08.1** is the release target. The user reported visual and primary-workflow testing passed before this final text-only pass. Automated regression and packaging evidence are in the accompanying release report; this is not a claim that every third-party combination or native feature was independently tested.

Ordinary review affects scheduling. Independent practice does not. Pip's **Introduce new cards** option can apply real Anki ratings after reveal. Timed practice deadlines continue while closed. **Save & close** is required to retain unfinished practice.

Anki Sync and its collection backup do not include all local Atelier data. Optional AI assistance requires its own service configuration and explicit approval. Source images and note content are not automatically fact-checked. See **USER-GUIDE.md** and **PRIVACY.md**.

Atelier has not been uploaded to AnkiWeb by this release process. The supplied installer updates the existing `daedalus_atelier` installation directly.

"""Read-only reviewer presentation decisions. No Anki or Qt dependency."""
from __future__ import annotations
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

PALETTES = json.loads((Path(__file__).parent / "web" / "palettes.json").read_text(encoding="utf8"))


def theme_tokens(theme: str) -> str:
    p = PALETTES.get(theme, PALETTES["obsidian"])
    return ":root{" + "".join(f"--at-{k}:{v};" for k, v in p.items()) + "}"


def plain_template(model: Any) -> bool:
    """Fail closed: only the small stock Basic/Cloze stylesheet is eligible.

    Translated model names are irrelevant. Custom CSS, scripts, occlusion,
    complex layouts and third-party note types retain their native card surface.
    Empty CSS is *not* assumed to mean safe: templates may depend on inheritance.
    """
    if not isinstance(model, dict):
        return False
    css = model.get("css", "")
    if not isinstance(css, str) or not css.strip():
        return False
    css = re.sub(r"/\*.*?\*/", "", css, flags=re.S)
    if "@" in css:
        return False
    rules = re.findall(r"([^{}]+)\{([^{}]*)\}", css)
    if not rules or re.sub(r"[^{}]+\{[^{}]*\}", "", css).strip():
        return False
    allowed = {
        ".card": {"font-family": {"arial", "arial, sans-serif"}, "font-size": {"20px"},
                  "text-align": {"center"}, "color": {"black", "#000", "#000000"},
                  "background-color": {"white", "#fff", "#ffffff"}},
        ".cloze": {"font-weight": {"bold"}, "color": {"blue", "#00f", "#0000ff"}},
        ".nightMode .cloze": {"color": {"lightblue"}},
        ".night_mode .cloze": {"color": {"lightblue"}},
    }
    seen_card = False
    for selector, body in rules:
        selector = " ".join(selector.split())
        if selector not in allowed:
            return False
        seen_card |= selector == ".card"
        for decl in body.split(";"):
            if not decl.strip():
                continue
            if ":" not in decl:
                return False
            prop, value = decl.split(":", 1)
            prop, value = prop.strip().lower(), " ".join(value.strip().lower().split())
            if value not in allowed[selector].get(prop, set()):
                return False
    templates = model.get("tmpls", [])
    if not isinstance(templates, list) or not templates:
        return False
    for tmpl in templates:
        if not isinstance(tmpl, dict):
            return False
        text = str(tmpl.get("qfmt", "")) + str(tmpl.get("afmt", ""))
        if re.search(r"<(?:script|style|canvas|svg|iframe|object|embed)\b|image.occlusion|io-overlay|io-wrapper", text, re.I):
            return False
    return seen_card


def static_text_template(model: Any) -> bool:
    """Eligible static custom text without touching scripted/positioned designs.

    The previous exact-stock CSS allow-list rejected ordinary formatted notes.
    This separate classifier allows headings, typography, lists, tables, cloze
    and typed-answer fields, but rejects positioning and interactive templates.
    Runtime media detection is an additional guard, not a substitute for this.
    """
    if not isinstance(model, dict) or not isinstance(model.get('tmpls'), list) or not model['tmpls']:
        return False
    text = ''.join(str(t.get('qfmt',''))+str(t.get('afmt','')) for t in model['tmpls'] if isinstance(t,dict))
    css = re.sub(r'/\*.*?\*/', '', str(model.get('css','')), flags=re.S)
    if not text.strip():
        return False
    if re.search(r'<(?:script|iframe|canvas|svg|object|embed|video|audio)\b|\bon[a-z]+\s*=|javascript:|image.?occlusion|io[-_]overlay|io[-_]wrapper', text, re.I):
        return False
    if re.search(r'(?:position\s*:\s*(?:absolute|fixed|sticky)|transform\s*:|zoom\s*:|@import|@keyframes|display\s*:\s*none|visibility\s*:\s*hidden|opacity\s*:\s*0(?:\D|$))', css+' '+text, re.I):
        return False
    return True
